title: A Giant Storm Soaks New York and New Jersey
summary:
Imagine a storm so big it stretches from Virginia all the way to Maine. That's what hit the northeastern United States on Saturday. It's called a nor'easter, and it brought flooding, strong winds, and heavy rain to tens of millions of people.

In New Jersey, streets and homes in towns like Surf City and Manasquan were covered in floodwater. More than 100,000 homes lost electricity. Airports were a mess too: more than 2,400 flights were delayed and 1,199 were cancelled. Even a football game and a big concert in Central Park were called off.

New York and New Jersey both declared states of emergency. That lets leaders act fast to help people. Governor Mikie Sherrill told everyone in New Jersey to "take this storm seriously." New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani had a simple warning: "Do not drive or walk through floodwater."

Why was the flooding so bad? Saturday night's full moon pulled the ocean higher than normal, pushing even more water onto the shore. That's a double whammy: storm plus full moon. Forecasters say the rain and wind will keep going through the weekend.
why_it_matters: Big coastal storms can close schools, cut off power, and make streets dangerous, so knowing the safety rule — never drive or walk through floodwater — helps keep you and your family safe.

background_read: A nor'easter is a big storm that forms along the U.S. East Coast. Its strongest winds blow in from the northeast, which is how it gets its name.
New York and New Jersey are states on the Atlantic Ocean (New Jersey sits just south of New York). When a storm pushes ocean water up onto land like this, it is called a 'storm surge'.
When a full moon makes the ocean's tides extra high, people sometimes call it a 'king tide' — that is why the moon made this flood even worse.
Article_Structure: WHO: Tens of millions of people in the northeastern U.S., including New Jersey Governor Mikie Sherrill and New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani.

WHAT: A nor'easter brought flooding, strong winds, and heavy rain — more than 100,000 homes lost power, more than 2,400 flights were delayed and 1,199 cancelled, and a football game and a Central Park concert were called off.
WHERE: From Virginia all the way to Maine, with towns like Surf City and Manasquan in New Jersey flooded and New York City also hit hard.
WHY: Saturday night's full moon pulled the ocean higher than normal, pushing even more water onto the shore, and forecasters say the rain and wind will keep going through the weekend.

perspectives.description: Governor Mikie Sherrill and Mayor Zohran Mamdani declared states of emergency so leaders could act fast, and both told people to take the storm seriously and stay out of the floodwater.
People whose streets and homes were covered in water, and the 100,000+ families who lost electricity, are dealing with damage and a weekend stuck indoors.
Forecasters point out that the storm's timing with the full moon made the flooding worse than it would normally be, and they warn the rain and wind are not over yet.
